work_items.title: Enforce two-phase planning/scheduling and execution automation loop
acceptance_criteria: Completed automation-run chat windows become planning/scheduling-only contexts unless the user explicitly overrides execution mode.
Fresh automation turns execute only already-scheduled runnable tasks first.
When no scheduled runnable tasks exist, a fresh automation turn plans unscheduled issues or user needs, schedules ready plans as tasks, records evidence, and ends its own turn.

If planning creates runnable scheduled tasks, the turn records closure evidence and triggers the next scheduler-visible automation turn instead of implementing those newly-created tasks in the same context.

Workflow, reusable templates, automation prompt guidance, hooks, validation checklist, state/progress/dashboard/backoff evidence, and target-repo upgrade guidance consistently describe the two-phase loop.
Coding tasks in Lambchop and Lambchop-enabled projects require the tdd skill contract: one public-behavior test first, minimal implementation to green, repeat, then refactor only while green.
Validation covers the failure mode where a chat only summarizes the loop without queuing work, and the failure mode where an automation both creates and executes the same task in one turn.
implementation_notes: Bill described Lambchop as a two-part process loop: post-automation chats plan/schedule; fresh automation turns execute scheduled tasks, or plan/schedule work when none are runnable, then trigger a new turn if runnable work was created.
Do not preserve the ambiguous current behavior where a single context can plan new work and immediately implement that same work.

Intake correction after Bill flagged that the prior response only described the two-phase loop and did not queue work. The new task schedules implementation of a strict planning/scheduling versus execution loop for Lambchop-enabled projects.

work_items.title: Make scheduler-visible run-now handoff terminal (no writes after trigger)
acceptance_criteria: After a scheduler-visible run-now trigger is executed, the automation turn must stop immediately (no more tool calls, edits, validation, commits, or ledger updates).
Intake chats must record and commit ledger/task evidence before triggering run-now; no evidence updates occur after the trigger.
Automation runs must perform validation, ledger updates, and commits before triggering the next run-now; the trigger is the last step.
Repo-local Stop hook blocks completion messages that imply work continued after run-now (e.g. 'triggered run-now then updated state/progress').
Validation adds at least one test proving the Stop hook blocks run-now + post-trigger-work evidence patterns.
Handoff evidence logs only that run-now was initiated (not that it ran); the next automation run confirms execution by recognizing itself.
No scheduler DB verification or run/thread confirmation is required in the initiating turn; avoid treating the current chat as the running automation context.
implementation_notes: Root cause: the 2026-05-20 intake entry triggered run-now and then continued with additional edits/validation/commits, which violates the contract that handoff must be terminal.
This guardrail should be a workflow + hook + test triple: explicit ordering rules, completion enforcement, and a failing test that proves the enforcement.
Bill clarified that handoff logging must record initiation only; do not log scheduler DB verification as completion evidence in the same turn.
